name: The verbal noun
definition: A noun that names the act itself, without a time, such as naṣr (helping) from naṣara.
body: نَصْرٌ (helping), ضَرْبٌ (striking), عِلْمٌ (knowing). For the bare three-letter verb the maṣdar is learnt by hearing; for the added patterns it follows a rule: تَعْلِيمٌ from عَلَّمَ, إِكْرَامٌ from أَكْرَمَ, اِسْتِغْفَارٌ from اِسْتَغْفَرَ.

The grammarians of Basra held that the maṣdar is the source from which the verb and the other forms are taken; those of Kufa held that the verb is the source. The name maṣdar, the place something issues from, reflects the Basran view.
